<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|136|THE GOSPEL|CHA. I.}}</noinclude>thou shalt conceiue in thy vvombe, and shalt beare a sonne: and thou shalt call his name {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=32}}† he shal be great, and shal be called the sonne of the most High, and our Lord God shal giue him the seate of Dauid his father: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=33}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Dan. 7, 14. 27.''}}* and he shal reigne in the house of Iacob for euer, and of his kingdom there shal be no end. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=34}}† And {{sc|Marie}} said to the Angel, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ She doubted not of the thing as Zacharie, but enquired of the meanes.}}∷ Hovv shal this be done? because {{sup|‖}} I knovv not man? {{verse|chapter=1|verse=35}}† And the Angel ansvvering, said to her, The Holy Ghost shal come vpon thee, and the povver of the most High shal ouershadovv thee. And therfore also that vvhich of thee shal be borne Holy, shal be called the sonne of God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=36}}† And behold {{sup|‖}} Elisabeth thy cosin, she also hath conceiued a sonne in her old age: and this moneth, is the sixt to her that is called barren: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=37}}† because there shal not be impossible vvith God any word. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=38}}† And {{sc|Marie}} said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ At this very moment when the B. Virgin gaue consent, she conceiued him perfect God and perfect man.}}∷ ''{{sc|Behold}} the handmaid of our Lord, be it done to me according to thy word''. ⊣ And the Angel departed from her.

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=39}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Visitatiō of our Lady, Iul. 2. And vpon the Imber friday in Aduent.}}And {{sc|Marie}} rising vp in those daies, vvent vnto the hil countrie vvith speede, into a citie of Iuda. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=40}}† and she entred into the house of Zacharie, and saluted Elisabeth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=41}}† And it came to passe: as Elisabeth heard the salutation of {{sc|Marie}}, the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Iohn the Baptist being yet in his mothers vvombe, reioyced and acknowledged the presence of Christ and his mother.}}∷ infant did leape in her vvombe. and Elisabeth vvas replenished vvith the Holy Ghost: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=42}}† and she cried out vvith a loude voice, and said, ''{{sup|‖}} {{sc|Blessed}} art thou among vvomen, and blessed is the fruite of thy vvombe''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=43}}† And vvhence is this to me, that the {{sup|‖}} mother of my Lord doth come to me? {{verse|chapter=1|verse=44}}† For behold as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine eares, the infant in my vvombe did leape for ioy. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=45}}† And blessed is she that beleeued, because those things shal be accomplished that vvere spoken to her by our Lord. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=46}}† And {{sc|Marie}} said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ MAGNIFICAT at Euensong.}}∷ ''MY {{sc|Sovle}} doth magnifie our Lord''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=47}}† ''And my spirit hath reioyced in God my Sauiour''.⊣

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=48}}† ''Because he hath regarded the humilitie of his handmaid: for behold from hence forth '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Haue the Protestants had alwaies generations to fulfil this prophecie? or do they call her blessed, that derogate what they can from her graces, blessings, and al her honour?}}∷ ''al generations {{sup|‖}} shal call me blessed''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=49}}† ''Because he that is mightie hath done great things to me, and holy is his name''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=50}}† ''And his mercie from generation vnto generations, to them that feare him''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=51}}† ''He hath shewed might in his arme: he hath dispersed the proude in the conceit of their hart''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=52}}† ''He hath deposed the mightie from their seate, and hath exalted the humble''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=53}}† ''The hungrie he hath filled vvith good things: and the riche he hath sent away emptie''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=54}}† ''He hath receiued Israel his childe, being mindeful of his mercie'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=55}}† ''As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham and his seede for euer''.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
